title: Search query parameter type confusion bypasses input bounds and triggers request failures
source: Anonymous GET /rest/products/search query parameter q; Express uses extended qs parsing, so q can be an object or array.
closest_control: Base lines 21-22 required typeof rawCriteria === 'string'; target line 21 removes that guard and assigns req.query.q to any.
sink: routes/search.ts:22 reads attacker-selected length and may call substring() on a non-string; arrays can also bypass the intended 200-character bound before interpolation into the SQL statement at line 23.
impact: Unauthenticated malformed requests can deterministically cause request-level TypeError/HTTP 500 responses; repeated-value arrays can bypass the 200-character query bound and amplify SQL parsing work. Process-wide availability impact is not yet established.
plausibility: The target exactly reintroduces code removed by commit 068a6b3396, whose stated purpose was fixing CodeQL alert 32, Type confusion through parameter tampering.
validation_proof_gap: Determine whether realistic malformed or oversized requests cause meaningful service-wide resource exhaustion beyond isolated 500 responses.

attack_path.dataflow: q query value -> req.query.q -> criteria -> length/substring operation and SQL interpolation
attack_path.sink_reachability: Direct and unconditional before database query execution
attack_path.reportability_note: Carry to validation; do not report the unchanged intentional SQL injection as a new diff finding.
